books.title_en: The Knight Who Laid Down His Sword

volumes.en:
Sir Alden returned from a battle with a broken shield. He expected a welcome, but the village square was empty. The people were repairing their homes. He put his sword beside the well and asked where he could help.

Alden found the well rope dragging in the mud and tied it to a post. A child pointed him toward a house whose door would no longer close.

기사 올든은 부서진 방패를 들고 전투에서 돌아왔다. 환영을 기대했지만 마을 광장은 비어 있었다. 주민들은 집을 수리하고 있었다. 그는 우물 옆에 검을 내려놓고 어디를 도우면 되는지 물었다.

올든은 우물 밧줄이 진흙에 끌리는 것을 보고 기둥에 묶었다. 한 아이가 문이 닫히지 않는 집을 가리켰다.

A carpenter named Nella gave Alden a hammer. He was strong, but he knew little about building houses. His first shelf fell to the floor. Nella showed him how to measure the wood, and he tried again.

They used the fallen shelf as a workbench rather than throwing it away. Alden handed Nella the ruler before he picked up the hammer again.

두 사람은 무너진 선반을 버리는 대신 작업대로 썼다. 올든은 다시 망치를 들기 전에 넬라에게 자를 건넸다.

A stranger arrived with the badge of a former enemy. Alden reached for his sword, but the stranger asked for water. Nella brought two cups. The men discovered that both had lost their homes in the war.

The stranger set his badge on the table where everyone could see it. Alden brought a chair and let him finish his story before asking how he had found the village.

낯선 이는 누구나 볼 수 있게 탁자 위에 휘장을 놓았다. 올든은 의자를 가져다주고 마을을 어떻게 찾아왔는지 묻기 전에 이야기를 끝까지 들었다.

The village had little grain left. Some people wanted to send the stranger away. Alden suggested sharing the remaining food while they asked nearby farms for help. The stranger offered to repair their mill.

The villagers counted the sacks before anyone made a promise. They put one bowl by the mill for the worker who would take the late shift.

Heavy rain flooded the lower road. Alden wanted to carry everyone across himself, but Nella organized a team. They used ropes and a boat to move the villagers to higher ground. No single person could have done it alone.

Nella assigned one person to watch the rope and another to count the people on the bank. Alden took the last trip only after the watcher gave the signal.

넬라는 한 사람에게 밧줄을 살피게 하고 다른 사람에게 강둑의 인원을 세게 했다. 올든은 감시자가 신호를 보낸 뒤에야 마지막 배를 탔다.

Alden's old commander came to recruit him. He promised a new shield and a place of honor. Alden looked at the unfinished houses. He asked the commander to leave the village workers in peace.

The commander asked whether a repaired roof was worth giving up a medal. Alden pointed through the doorway to the family eating supper beneath it.

The villagers built a bell tower to warn people of floods. Alden donated the metal from his broken shield. When the bell rang for the first time, he heard children laughing in the square. He felt proud of something he had helped build.

Before the first storm, children practiced walking from the square to higher ground. Their parents wrote down how long the route took while the road was still dry.

Many years later, a young knight asked Alden about his greatest victory. Alden pointed to the bridge, the mill, and the houses. The young knight wrote down their names instead of the names of battles. That was how the village remembered Alden.

The visitor found Nella’s mark on the doorframe and added her name beside Alden’s. By dusk, the list also held the names of the rope keepers and the people who had baked bread.

books.title_en: The Girl Who Followed the Stars

volumes.en:
Lina watched the stars from her father's roof. She drew their positions in a notebook every evening. Her brother laughed at the little dots, but she noticed that some stars appeared in the same places each season.

Lina began marking not just the stars but the hour when she saw them. When her brother borrowed the notebook, he found that he could reproduce one of her drawings.
volumes.ko:
리나는 아버지 집 지붕에서 별을 관찰했다. 매일 저녁 공책에 별의 위치를 그렸다. 오빠는 작은 점들을 보고 웃었지만 리나는 어떤 별들이 계절마다 같은 위치에 나타난다는 것을 알아차렸다.

리나는 별뿐 아니라 그것을 본 시각도 기록하기 시작했다. 오빠가 수첩을 빌려 보니 그림 하나를 그대로 따라 그릴 수 있었다.

A fishing boat failed to return before dark. Lina asked the harbor keeper how sailors found their way at night. He showed her an old chart. She began to compare the chart with her notebook.

The chart showed a light at the mouth of the harbor, but its ink had almost worn away. Lina asked the keeper to mark where the light could be seen from the water.

해도에는 항구 입구의 등불이 표시되어 있었지만 잉크가 거의 지워져 있었다. 리나는 물 위 어느 지점에서 등불이 보이는지 표시해 달라고 했다.

Lina offered to guide a short practice voyage. Clouds covered the sky, and she could not see her stars. The captain returned to the harbor using familiar coastal landmarks. Lina added a warning to her notebook: never depend on one kind of sign.

They wrote down the time when each headland disappeared in the mist. Back on shore, Lina added those observations beside her clear-weather drawings.

The group wrote each contributor’s name and date beside the new markings. A sailor who found an error could then tell which observation to check.

Lina began teaching children how to read simple charts. One student asked why the moon changed shape. She did not know the answer, so they observed it together for a month. Their new drawings filled an entire wall.

They left the wall blank on nights when clouds hid the moon. A student suggested using a different mark for something observed and something predicted.

When Lina grew old, her students carried copies of the chart to other ports. She kept the first notebook in a wooden box. On its last page she wrote that a good map should help its readers ask better questions.

The first copy that came back from another port had a new note about a sandbar. Lina smiled to see that the chart was still changing after it left her hands.

volumes.en:
A young archivist named Tavin found a portrait with no name beneath it. The crown was clear, but the face had faded. He asked the keeper whether the king had been forgotten. The keeper handed him a box of records.

Tavin copied the markings on the frame before he opened the box. That gave him a record of what he had actually seen.

One repair account mentioned cloth and gold paint. It did not connect either purchase to the portrait.

Tavin drew the position of the note before removing it. Its place behind the frame was as important as the words it contained.

Rain began to fall through the roof above the history shelves. Sera called the other workers instead of trying to move every book alone. They formed a line and carried the books to a dry room. The youngest helper saved the shelf labels.

The workers counted the stacks as they crossed the corridor. When the rain stopped, they knew which shelves still needed attention.

일꾼들은 복도를 건널 때마다 책 더미의 수를 셌다. 비가 그쳤을 때는 어느 책장을 더 살펴야 하는지 알고 있었다.

While drying the books, Sera found a copy with no source note. It looked older than the others, but its paper was new. She placed it in a separate folder and asked a specialist to examine it.

The folder included a note stating what Sera had seen and what she had only guessed. The specialist returned it with a description of the paper fibers.

A visitor wanted the library to destroy a letter that embarrassed his family. Sera listened to him and offered to restrict access to private details. She explained that a public historical record could not simply disappear. They agreed to review the letter together.

They marked which details concerned living members of the family. The public description still listed the date and purpose of the letter.

volumes.en:
A storm damaged the road, and most workers could not reach the library. Sera opened only the safe reading room. She asked visitors to return the books themselves and kept a list of every loan. The library remained useful even with fewer services.

A visitor made an extra return slip for someone who could not write easily. Sera placed the slip beside the list instead of asking the visitor to stand aside.

한 방문객은 글쓰기가 어려운 사람을 위해 반납표를 한 장 더 만들었다. 세라는 그 방문객을 물러서게 하는 대신 표를 목록 옆에 놓았다.

Sera sent copies of useful books to villages beyond the damaged road. Each copy included its source and date. A village teacher returned a page of corrections with reasons for each one. Sera added the notes without destroying the earlier version.

The next edition printed the reasons in the margin. A reader could still find the page number in the older copy.

On her final night before retirement, Sera found a child reading beside the last lamp. The child asked who would protect the books after she left. Sera pointed to the other readers and the new librarians. She said the library had never belonged to one keeper.

The child left a bookmark where the next reader could find the page. Sera entered the loan before she turned off the last lamp.

The next morning, the new librarian unlocked the door. Sera entered as an ordinary reader and borrowed a book about the sea. Her name was no longer on the duty list, but her notes remained in the catalog. The work continued.

The new librarian asked Sera to sign the loan card just like anyone else. Sera took the book to the window and began reading.
